name: M24C02-WMN6TP
title: 1-Kbit and 2-Kbit I2C serial EEPROM (M24C01-W/R, M24C02-W/R, M24C02-F)
summary: Byte-wide I2C EEPROM family: the M24C01 holds 128 bytes (1 Kbit) and the M24C02 256 bytes (2 Kbit), written in 16-byte pages with a 5 ms maximum write cycle. Three supply grades exist: W runs from 2.5 V to 5.5 V, R from 1.8 V to 5.5 V, and F (M24C02 only) from 1.7 V to 5.5 V, or down to 1.6 V over a narrower temperature span. All run the bus at up to 400 kHz over -40 °C to 85 °C, have three chip-enable pins that set the low bits of the device select code, and a WC pin that blocks writes to the whole array. The M24C02-WMN6TP is the 2-Kbit, 2.5 V to 5.5 V part in SO8N on tape and reel.

Device grade 6: industrial, tested with the standard flow over -40 °C to 85 °C.
Plating P or G: ECOPACK, RoHS compliant. PDIP8 is ECOPACK1 (RoHS); SO8, TSSOP8 and UFDFPN8 are ECOPACK2 (RoHS and halogen-free).

circuits.title: I2C bus with pull-up Rbus and bus capacitance Cbus
circuits.description: A bus master and the EEPROM share SCL and SDA. SDA is pulled up to VCC through Rbus, and Cbus is the total parasitic capacitance of the line to ground. Rbus is picked from the Rbus-versus-Cbus graph so that Rbus × Cbus stays under 400 ns at 400 kHz, for example 4 kΩ with 30 pF.
notes: E2, E1, E0 and WC are open: open chip-enable inputs read as 0 and an open WC leaves writes enabled.

equations.name: Device select code
equations.expr: device select code = 1010 E2 E1 E0 RW (b7 first)

where.E2, E1, E0: levels on the chip enable pins

operation.text: VCC must be inside the operating range and steady before the device is selected, and stay so until the instruction is sent and, for a write, until the internal cycle tW ends. A 10 nF to 100 nF capacitor close to the VCC and VSS pins keeps the supply steady.
VCC must climb monotonically from 0 V to the minimum operating voltage, no faster than 1 V/µs.

A power-on-reset circuit guards against stray writes. Until VCC passes its internal threshold, which sits below the minimum operating voltage, the device ignores all instructions; past it the device resets into Standby. It should still not be addressed until VCC is inside the operating range. Going down, it should not be addressed below VCC(min), and below the threshold it stops responding.
While VCC falls the device must be in Standby: a Stop condition has been decoded and no internal write is under way.
The device is always a slave on the I2C bus; the master starts every transfer and drives SCL.

Start is SDA falling while SCL is high; every instruction begins with one, and the device watches for it at all times except during a write cycle. Stop is SDA rising while SCL is high; it ends the exchange, puts the device in Standby after a read ended with NoAck, and starts the internal write cycle when it closes a Write instruction.

SDA is sampled on the SCL rising edge, so it must be stable then and change only while SCL is low. After eight data bits the transmitter releases SDA and the receiver pulls it low on the ninth clock to acknowledge.

After Start the master sends the device select code MSB first: 1010, then the three chip-enable bits, then RW (1 read, 0 write). A device whose E2-E1-E0 pins match acknowledges on the ninth bit; any other deselects itself and goes to Standby.
With WC high the device still acknowledges the device select and address bytes but refuses (NoAck) every data byte, and the array is not changed. WC low or open allows writes.
Device select with RW = 0, address byte, one data byte, then Stop. The device acknowledges each byte; a write-protected location gets NoAck on the data byte and is left alone.

Up to 16 bytes go in one write cycle provided all of them lie in one page (their upper address bits are equal). Each byte advances the internal page counter; bytes beyond the last location of a page wrap round to location 0 of that page. The master ends the transfer with Stop.

The internal write cycle tW starts only when Stop comes right after a data byte's acknowledge (the 10th bit slot); Stop at any other point starts nothing. During tW SDA is disconnected inside and the device answers nothing. Afterwards the address counter points to the byte after the last one written.

tW max is 5 ms but the typical cycle is shorter. To finish sooner the master can send Start and the device select code repeatedly: no acknowledge means the cycle is still running; an acknowledge means it is done and the select code just sent counts as the first byte of the next instruction.

Reads work whatever the WC level. After each byte out the device waits for an acknowledge on the ninth bit; without one it stops sending and enters Standby. After a read the address counter steps by one.

A dummy write (device select with RW = 0 and the address byte, no Stop) loads the address; then a repeated Start, device select with RW = 1, and the device sends that byte. The master returns NoAck and a Stop.
Start and device select with RW = 1 only; the device sends the byte at its internal counter and the counter increments. The master answers NoAck and sends Stop.
After a current or random address read, the master acknowledges each byte and keeps clocking to get consecutive addresses; NoAck plus Stop ends it. Past the last address the counter wraps to 00h.
Every bit is 1 as shipped: each byte reads FFh.

SDA is open drain and needs a pull-up Rbus to VCC. At 400 kHz the product of Rbus and the line capacitance Cbus must be under 400 ns, which sets the largest allowed Rbus for a given Cbus (40 kΩ at 10 pF down to 1 kΩ at 400 pF).
The centre pad is pulled to VSS inside the package; on the board it connects to VSS or nothing, never to another voltage or signal.
